nodes.rationale: input_entities and output_entities are combined as sorted(set(input_entities) | set(output_entities)) rather than concatenation, because redact() itself already returns a sorted/deduped list, and audit_logger joins entities in caller order without re-sorting — so the pipeline is the one place that must both dedupe (an entity masked on both sides is one type, not two) and sort (so the stored/serialized order is deterministic across Presidio versions).

nodes.label: Additive-only API contract discipline
nodes.rationale: pii_redacted/pii_entities_masked are added to QuerySuccessResponse only, computed by hoisting the already-existing merged-entity expression into a shared local (masked_entities) so the audit column and the API signal are always the same fact told to two audiences and can never silently drift apart. QueryRequest and the two BLOCKED response models are left completely untouched — redaction never becomes a distinct new leak surface or a breaking request-contract change.

nodes.label: Executable isolation guarantee for dedup/pattern checks
nodes.norm_label: executable isolation guarantee for dedup/pattern checks
nodes.rationale: Turns RF-6's promise ('duplicate_checker.py is untouched, dedup hash always computed over raw text') from an absence-of-change assumption into an executable test, because two distinct prompts were measured to collide to the identical masked string — if redacted text were ever routed into check_duplicate() or log_query(prompt=...), a second user's legitimate request would be silently blocked as a duplicate with no error and no trace. A test-only story; no app code is modified.

nodes.label: Telemetry exposure without a new leak surface
nodes.norm_label: telemetry exposure without a new leak surface
nodes.rationale: GET /audit and GET /stats gain pii_detected_input/output, pii_entities, pii_detected_queries and top_pii_entities, but the story deliberately declines to also add prompt_preview/response_preview to /audit even though the literal AC wording implies it, because that would push raw PII of the last 100 requests into a single admin JSON payload — a genuine expansion of the leak surface the epic exists to close, not merely an oversight to fix in passing.

nodes.label: Four-surface end-to-end consistency proof
nodes.rationale: Earlier stories proved each pipeline step in isolation; none asserted that the outbound OpenRouter payload, the HTTP response body, the persisted audit row, and the /audit+/stats admin view all agree about the very same single request. A three-entity prompt and response are used deliberately (not a single EMAIL_ADDRESS) so a regression that drops one entity type from the union cannot pass unnoticed. Test-only story; no app code is modified.

nodes.label: Reflex lifespan-bypass warm-load compensation
nodes.rationale: Reflex's api_transformer mounts fastapi_app under an outer Starlette app whose own lifespan runs instead, so app.main's lifespan (and STORY-002's pii_redactor.load()) never fires inside the container — the same bypass that already forced init_db() to be called eagerly. The fix registers load as a Reflex lifespan task (not an eager import-time call), so the discarded Docker builder stage never pays for the 425MB spaCy model download while the running container still warm-loads it before serving traffic.

nodes.label: Docs must mirror shipped code, not the PRD draft
nodes.norm_label: docs must mirror shipped code, not the prd draft
nodes.rationale: Every documented env var, response field and example value is cross-checked against the actual shipped app/config.py, app/models/schemas.py and app/routers/admin.py rather than the PRD's pre-implementation draft, because the PRD's own /audit example shows a prompt_preview field the endpoint has never returned (STORY-009 deliberately excluded it) — documenting the draft instead of the shipped contract would ship an inaccurate README.

nodes.label: asyncio.to_thread offload of blocking pipeline call
nodes.norm_label: asyncio.to_thread offload of blocking pipeline call
nodes.rationale: The synchronous run_query(...) call inside ChatState.send() is wrapped in await asyncio.to_thread(...) so a slow OpenRouter call runs on a worker thread instead of blocking the single Reflex event loop, keeping every other session's page responsive while one session's request is in flight. Chosen over restructuring run_query() itself, so behavior, exceptions and output stay byte-for-byte identical (no visual change in this story).

nodes.label: No-silent-drops exception handling principle
nodes.rationale: ChatState.send() gains a PiiRedactorError arm and a catch-all except Exception arm so that every possible failure from the threaded run_query() call terminates in a visible system bubble instead of the user's message silently vanishing with no feedback — 'no silent drops' from PRD Section 2 is treated as an exhaustiveness requirement over exception types, not just the two originally handled.

nodes.label: pending flag with finally-reset invariant guard
nodes.norm_label: pending flag with finally-reset invariant guard
nodes.rationale: pending: bool is set True before the threaded run_query() call and reset in a finally block wrapping every one of the six possible outcomes (success, duplicate, suspicious, OpenRouterError, PiiRedactorError, arbitrary Exception), guaranteeing the flag never gets stuck True. A second guard (`if self.pending: return`) rejects a concurrent send from the same session before it starts.

nodes.label: ChatMessage typed discriminated-union model
nodes.rationale: Replaces list[dict[str, str]] messages with a typed rx.Base model carrying a `kind` discriminator plus every metadata field (model_used, tokens_used, audit_id, pii_redacted, pii_entities, pattern, first_query_at, detail), so each of the six pipeline outcomes is distinguishable in state instead of being flattened into one formatted string, enabling later stories (metadata population, kind-based rendering) to build on a stable typed shape.

nodes.label: Full outcome-metadata surfacing (no discarded fields)
nodes.rationale: send() is updated to populate every field each pipeline result type actually carries (6 of 6 QuerySuccessResponse fields instead of 1) rather than collapsing outcomes into a pre-formatted f-string, and separates user-facing copy labels from raw exception detail text, so the UI stops silently discarding information the backend already computed.

nodes.label: Centralized copy module pattern
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing string (bubble labels, PII badge template, footer separators, retry/edit-resend labels, empty state, composer placeholder) is centralized in chat_ui/copy.py so changing display language or wording is a single-file edit; the PII badge copy is required to describe masking as covering 'this exchange' rather than only the user's prompt, and the duplicate-bubble copy must state the text must change for a resend to go through.

nodes.label: rx.match dispatch by message.kind
nodes.rationale: Six distinct renderers (user, assistant, duplicate, injection, upstream_error, internal_error) replace a legacy nested rx.cond over three roles, dispatched by a single rx.match on message.kind with a default fallback arm, so no two semantically different outcomes share a bubble style and an unknown kind still renders a visible bubble instead of nothing.

nodes.label: Informational, non-blocking PII badge
nodes.rationale: A quiet inline badge on assistant bubbles shows the masked entity types (never raw values) when pii_redacted is true, deliberately never as a modal, confirmation step, or gate — matching PRD's 'inform, don't obstruct' principle so users understand why a response might read <PERSON> instead of a name.

nodes.label: Subdued success metadata footer
nodes.rationale: Assistant bubbles show a visually subdued footer (model_used, tokens_used, audit_id) so usage is not invisible and a support request can quote an exact audit row id instead of a paraphrase, while remaining styled to never compete with the response text for attention.

nodes.label: Actionable duplicate-block feedback
nodes.rationale: The duplicate card shows a humanized relative time plus absolute timestamp and the computed 24-hour window release time (first_query_at + 24h), with a robust fallback that never crashes on an empty or unparseable timestamp ('no silent drops'), turning a bare rejection into an actionable explanation of when the block lifts.

nodes.label: Pending indicator + composer lock UX
nodes.rationale: While ChatState.pending is True, a typing/loading indicator renders at the end of the message list and the composer's text input and send button are disabled, so a slow OpenRouter call reads as visible progress rather than a frozen page; both reset automatically once pending flips back to False via STORY-003's finally guarantee.

nodes.label: Auto-scroll to newest message
nodes.rationale: The plain overflow-y:auto rx.box is replaced with Reflex's rx.auto_scroll so newly appended messages of any of the six kinds, plus the pending indicator, are automatically scrolled into view, preventing a reply that lands below the fold from appearing invisible.

nodes.norm_label: redesigned shell: header + designed empty state

nodes.norm_label: block-then-return audit pattern (log_query then typed blocked response)

nodes.label: ADMIN_TOKEN break-glass identity
nodes.rationale: ADMIN_TOKEN resolves via secrets.compare_digest to a synthetic admin Identity without ever touching the users table, so it works even if the users table is empty, missing, or buggy (break-glass access). Deliberately NOT sufficient to satisfy the startup bootstrap guard (STORY-016's check_bootstrap ignores ADMIN_TOKEN and checks count_active_users() instead), since a deployment with only a break-glass credential and zero real users would leave every other identity unresolvable.

nodes.label: Deny-by-default authorization
nodes.rationale: Authorization is deny-by-default: any role absent from ROLE_PERMISSIONS or any permission not explicitly granted raises PermissionDenied rather than falling back to a default grant. Chosen so an unmapped role/permission fails closed instead of open; RBAC_ENABLED=false is the single documented bypass, preserving pre-RBAC PRD-001 behavior as a migration escape hatch.

nodes.label: Fail-fast RBAC bootstrap guard (check_bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: check_bootstrap() raises RbacNotBootstrappedError when RBAC_ENABLED=true and count_active_users()==0, naming the exact scripts/manage_users.py create-user command to fix it. It deliberately does not treat a configured ADMIN_TOKEN as sufficient bootstrap, since identity.resolve() can synthesize an admin identity from ADMIN_TOKEN without any row in the users table -- so a deployment could otherwise appear to boot successfully while being usable only via one break-glass credential and unusable for anyone else.

nodes.label: Wholesale-replace RBAC_ROLES_FILE override (no merge)
nodes.rationale: authz.load() replaces ROLE_PERMISSIONS wholesale from RBAC_ROLES_FILE's JSON, never merging with the built-in matrix, so a permission the file omits for a role is denied rather than silently inherited from the default. A malformed file, an unreadable file, or a permission name outside the five known constants fails startup loudly (AuthzConfigError) instead of silently falling back to the built-in matrix, because a silent fallback would mean an operator's intended override is quietly not enforced.

nodes.label: libsql==0.1.11 Driver Decision
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is the only actively maintained client with the required remote-HTTP topology; three of six risky behaviors pass outright, commit semantics pass via the existing `with` idiom, and the two failures (named-column access, batch execution) have workarounds proven against the live endpoint. libsql-client was rejected despite offering named rows and batch() because it was archived; pyturso rejected as embedded and the wrong topology; turso-serverless not evaluated since the gate (no acceptable workaround) was never reached.

nodes.label: app/db/errors.py Module-Owned Exception Surface
nodes.rationale: Introduces StorageError / MissingRelationError / IntegrityError so only one function (_translated() in database.py) ever names a driver exception class, decoupling every other module from sqlite3 before the driver is swapped -- designed so STORY-006 could measure the swap against a green baseline instead of a remembered one.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL / TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN Pydantic Validators
nodes.rationale: Removes the sqlite:///harness_ai.db default outright, not merely replaces it, so a misconfigured deployment fails at import instead of silently writing to an ephemeral container layer; requires TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN whenever the endpoint is remote and never echoes the token in any validation message.

nodes.label: Process-Wide Shared libSQL Client
nodes.rationale: Measured, not assumed, that a per-thread client cache -- the plan's supposedly safe default -- actually loses writes under contention (7/8 threads hit TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT, only 29-31/200 rows durable), while one client shared by all threads was safe (0 errors, 200/200 rows durable). The defensive-looking design was the dangerous one; the correct design is the single process-wide client the acceptance criteria literally asked for.

nodes.label: Concurrency-Safe _add_missing_columns()
nodes.rationale: Treats a duplicate ADD COLUMN failure ('column already exists') as success and re-raises everything else, so the process that loses the read-then-ALTER race converges instead of crashing at import; proved with eight real processes booting simultaneously (8/8 exit 0 with the fix versus 5-6/8 exit 1 without it).

nodes.label: DB_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED Flag
nodes.rationale: Gates both the startup reachability guard and schema bootstrap so `reflex export` / `docker build` can import the app with no database reachable, while a running deployment still fails fast and legibly on an unreachable endpoint or bad token. Provided by STORY-008 for STORY-014 to set at build time.

nodes.label: STREAM_EXPIRED Idle Hrana Stream Defect
nodes.rationale: The process-wide shared libSQL client's Hrana stream expires after an idle window (a ~20s presidio/spaCy model load is enough), after which every later database access in that process fails with STREAM_EXPIRED. STORY-015 later found it does not self-recover and surfaces in the running application as a permanent 500 on every request, not merely a test-suite annoyance. Repeatedly flagged as needing its own story and repeatedly deferred; STORY-016 did not reproduce it because its instances are pinged continuously and never idle long enough to trigger it.

nodes.label: Finding: Test Suite Could Reach the Production Database
nodes.norm_label: finding: test suite could reach the production database
nodes.rationale: monkeypatch.undo() in one test reverted the autouse safety fixture that redirects settings.DATABASE_URL, letting a later statement in that same test run against whatever DATABASE_URL the container actually inherited -- which, once docker-compose.yml's env_file carried real Turso credentials, was production. Verified by controlled comparison (forced dev-server URL: 97 passed; inherited production URL: assert 17 == 1). Flagged as needing its own regression test before STORY-016, which runs two instances against one database using the same credential-handling shape.

nodes.label: Chat Session Ownership Rule (user_id scoping)
nodes.rationale: Every store function takes a required, undefaulted user_id, and every statement over an existing row carries WHERE user_id = ?, so a foreign session is indistinguishable from a missing one; ids are minted server-side with uuid4 so a client can never name a primary key. nodes.label: Single-file token guarantee
nodes.rationale: Every colour, size and face the console needs comes from chat_ui/theme.py; any new token is added there and nowhere else, preserving the single-file guarantee PRD-004 established for the chat surface.

nodes.label: Gate as state, not as route
nodes.norm_label: gate as state, not as route
nodes.rationale: The admin pages exist unconditionally; Reflex has no server-side route guard here, so the token check is expressed as the render condition itself, and data is not loaded until it passes.

nodes.label: Stamp margin signature
nodes.rationale: A narrow fixed-width left column carries each non-cleared row's verdict as a solid mark in its own ink, blank for cleared rows, so a hundred rows resolve into a vertical stripe of exceptions — finding the denied entries becomes a glance at an edge rather than a read of a table.

nodes.label: Three distinct register states
nodes.rationale: Nothing recorded, nothing matching the filter, and rows shown are rendered as three distinct states, checked in that order relative to a failed read, so a blank table is never ambiguous and a failure is never presented as emptiness.

nodes.label: Ruled tally sheet structure
nodes.rationale: The nine StatsResponse figures are set as a ruled list, not a grid of cards. blocked_duplicates and blocked_suspicious are indented beneath total_queries because they are a subset of it, and indentation states that relationship honestly where a card grid would falsely assert all figures as peers.

nodes.label: app/ untouched invariant
nodes.rationale: The console is confined to chat_ui/ with no new FastAPI route, no schema migration, no new query parameter and no new dependency; git diff main --stat shows no file under app/ changed, and the pre-existing test suite passes unmodified as the proof.

nodes.label: Risk 2: no preview fields on AuditRow
nodes.norm_label: risk 2: no preview fields on auditrow
nodes.rationale: AuditRow is a deliberate projection of AuditLog carrying no field for either prompt_preview or response_preview, so both are dropped at the boundary rather than being one binding away from the screen. The absence itself is the mitigation — the fields must not be added 'for completeness'.

nodes.label: Derived-once row model
nodes.rationale: Every displayed value on a register row is computed once in Python when the row is built (in admin_formatting.to_audit_row), never at render time, because Reflex component functions receive Vars, not values — the same reason PRD-004 put format_duplicate_info in formatting.py.

nodes.label: Risk 3: verdict never branches on model_used
nodes.norm_label: risk 3: verdict never branches on model_used
nodes.rationale: The obvious way to separate an upstream failure from an internal one is to check whether a model was recorded — and it is wrong, because the output-side PiiRedactorError arm logs a model_used value even on a failed row. derive_verdict never branches on model_used, and this reasoning is recorded in a module comment so the 'improvement' is not reintroduced.

nodes.label: Verdict derivation precedence
nodes.rationale: derive_verdict follows a fixed precedence so two rows with identical fields never render differently: was_duplicate_blocked -> held; suspicious_pattern is not None -> denied; success = 0 -> fault; otherwise cleared.

nodes.label: No-oracle gate refusal
nodes.rationale: An empty token, a wrong-length token and a wrong token of the correct length all produce the identical gate_error string, and authenticate() compares with secrets.compare_digest after consistent encoding, so no oracle (message or otherwise) distinguishes why authentication failed.

nodes.label: Risk 1: load() guarded by authentication
nodes.rationale: AdminState.load() returns immediately and performs no database read when the state is unauthenticated, so an unauthenticated page has no data in state regardless of what renders — the guard clause defined at the state layer, ahead of and independent from the render-level gate.

nodes.label: Risk 5: computed-var filter performance
nodes.rationale: Every keystroke in the filter re-evaluates visible_rows, a computed var over the full loaded row list. The mitigation is that 100 rows is a hard ceiling and the data is already in state; debouncing the input is an acceptable UI-local fallback, but a database-side filter is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: Risk 6: no cards, no accent colour
nodes.norm_label: risk 6: no cards, no accent colour
nodes.rationale: The KPI-cards-over-striped-table default is the strongest pull in this design space, and the drift arrives one reasonable-looking component at a time, usually as a Radix card imported for convenience. The console introduces no card, no fill and no accent colour beyond the inherited palette, enforced by render invariant tests.

nodes.label: Risk 4: scope labeling avoids contradiction
nodes.rationale: A summary that says '3,180 queries' beside a register showing 100 rows reads as a contradiction unless every figure states its scope — all-time over the whole table versus the register's last-100 window. The completion label is additionally pinned by a copy test so its wording cannot regress to 'success rate'.
